utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Madam Court Deputy, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Thank you. Examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record, Mr. Manning?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: My full name is Dean Paul Manning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you are currently working as a team leader in the Investigations Team at the ICTY, is that right?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to coming here you worked in Australia?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was a member and still am a member of the Australian federal police based in Canberra. I joined in 1993. The majority of my career has been involved in the investigation of serious crimes against persons and property such as murder, rape, armed robbery, serious theft, and serious drug offences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start working at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I joined the ICTY Srebrenica investigation in August of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your role in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I was an investigator with the Srebrenica team on general investigations. But specifically I was tasked with coordinating the exhumation activities of the team in relation to the Srebrenica-related mass graves and execution points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, please make a pause since you and the witness speak the same language. There is some difficulties for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I will bear that in mind, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Manning, is -- could you perhaps tell us more specifically what you were doing on the exhumations project.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhumation project had commenced in 1996, before I arrived. I was tasked with reviewing the previous exhumations and then coordinating the investigative efforts in relation to those exhumations and the autopsy efforts at the Visoko morgue. Effectively I attended the exhumation sites along with other investigators and also the mortuary complex. I coordinated other investigators who monitored the exhumations. I attended the morgue and collected evidence. I selected what evidence would be returned to the Tribunal. I returned that evidence to the Tribunal. I also facilitated the return and transfer of bodies to the Bosnian government. I was also required to facilitate the work of the experts employed by the ICTY in relation to those exhumations and to assist them in producing reports for the team and for presentation in court. The activities were basically to coordinate our investigative efforts with the exhumations and autopsy teams and experts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand you prepared a curriculum vitae outlining your background in order to save time?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is Exhibit 551? I believe it's on your screen. Is that your curriculum vitae, Mr. Manning?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, it is -- yes, it was. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, what were the objectives of the exhumation project?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: There were a number of general objectives and clearly specific objectives. One of the objectives was to corroborate and account for the witness or survivor testimonies in relation to the execution sites and mass graves which were detailed by survivors and witnesses. It was to provide a definitive count of the number of victims and also to provide a -- an assessment of cause of death, gender, age, and any other details which could be obtained from the examination of the remains. Also to provide ultimately a number of the bodies represented in the graves and from the execution points. And to identify, if possible, offenders and to identify the victims, if possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you and your team examine evidence found at killing sites that were not mass graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. Specifically two execution points were examined in 1996 by the U.S. Naval investigation service prior to my working at the Tribunal. We also examined other suspected execution sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Identify those sites?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The two sites examined by the U.S. Naval investigations service in 1996 were the Pilica Dom to the north of Srebrenica and an agricultural warehouse known as the Kravica warehouse to the south of -- to the -- in the area of Srebrenica near Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you been present during some or all of the exhumations of the mass grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've attended all the mass grave sites. Obviously the ones exhumed before I commenced duty I attended the site after they had been exhumed. I attended a number of exhumations whilst they were being conducted. And I also attended the execution points of the Pilica Dom and the Kravica warehouse. The Kravica warehouse I have attended on a large number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate what years the exhumations were conducted in in respect of the Srebrenica investigation.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Exhumations were conducted on four sites in 1996. In 1997 there were no Srebrenica-related exhumations. In 1998, eight sites were exhumed, one primary site and seven secondary sites. 1999, 2000, and 2001, exhumations continued, 2001 being the last exhumations conducted by ICTY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I understand, Mr. Manning, that you prepared reports detailing the results of the exhumations that were conducted. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct. At -- to assist the investigations team and also for presentation in Court, I produced three reports based on the work of the experts involved in the exhumations and autopsy process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record those reports are at Exhibits 552, 553, and 554 and they have already been admitted by this Chamber, pursuant to the ruling on November 7th, 2003. Now, Mr. Manning, in addition to your direct experience from the work you've described, what material did you use in preparing your reports?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: As I said, I based my reports on an examination of the expert reports produced including the anthropological, pathology, exhumation and other expert reports. I also examined a large number of documents produced by that work, the autopsy reports, the data collected at exhumation sites, the photographs collected at the exhumations and autopsy process, which were about 65.000 photographs. As I said, I also selected and examined the exhibits produced from the exhumations and autopsies and returned those to the Tribunal and placed them into the evidence. So it was an examination of the reports and the artifacts and my being present at the exhumation/autopsy processes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what type of experts worked on this project?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: There were a number of experts engaged by the OTP, specifically archaeologists, including a chief archaeologists, pathologists, anthropologists, experts in various fields in relation to the fields of examination of human remains, such as forensic dentistry, x-ray, and similar experts. We also employed a number of on-site experts, such as former police or serving police officers who controlled the exhibits and the bodies which were removed from the graves. Also at the mortuary, police photographers, and evidence handlers were employed. We also tasked specific experts such as Dr. Tony Brown who was a palaeonologist, a soil expert. We also deployed a DNA, cloth, textile, DNA -- sorry, explosives and other types of experts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand again for ease of reference you prepared a chart detailing the experts that were used by the OTP for the purposes of the exhumations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct. It lists the expert and the report that they produced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's at Exhibit 646?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then, Mr. Manning, to the specific grave sites, can you indicate what are the total number of grave sites associated with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: At the moment we know of 43 mass grave sites in total. 23 of those had been exhumed by ICTY. The remainder were handed over to the Bosnian Commission for Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are there any graves that have not been exhumed as such?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: We handed over the remaining 20 graves to the Bosnia commission, which were all secondary graves which we were unable to exhume. They, along with the International Commission for Missing Persons, have been exhuming those graves. Initially the ICTY monitored that process, but in 2002 we stopped doing that and the Bosnian commission continues to exhume those graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I understand, Mr. Manning, you also prepared a chart outlining the examined and exhumed graves, and that's at Exhibit 647. Can you just go through this chart for us and indicate what it represents.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a table which indicates the graves on the left which have been exhumed by ICTY. In 1996, four graves are listed. In 1998, the eight graves are listed. And so on from 1991, 2000, 2001. In 2001, we also exhumed or monitored the exhumation of the Ravnice 2 with the Bosnian Commission and the International Commission for Missing Persons. The graves on the left-hand side which are bold indicate primary graves and the others are secondary graves. On the right-hand side is a list of graves which are all secondary graves which were probed or tested to determine if they contained bodies. They were tested and found to contain multiple human remains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you -- and you also make a distinction between primary graves and secondary graves. Can you indicate what that distinction is, what's the difference?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Primary graves are graves in which the people or the victims were initially placed after their death or indeed were executed whilst in the graves or near the graves. The other graves, the secondary graves, are those graves which have been created since that time and the bodies from the primary graves have been moved to the secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also indicated that the secondary graves -- or rather, the examined by unexhumed graves are -- were tested somehow to determine that they are graves. Can you elaborate on that.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, the graves were identified using an archaeologist and aerial imagery, which no doubt we'll will speak of later. Once the outline or the area of the grave was tentatively identified either by hand digging or, more commonly, mechanical digging, a trench was put through the area of the grave or trenches were dug in various parts of the grave until human remains were located and it was considered that it would have to be multiple remains of multiple individuals to qualify as a mass grave. So samples, if you like, were examined from various parts of the grave. And if sufficient remains were found, it was deemed to be a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I also note that on your chart you have an indication of a disturbed primary mass grave. You may have touched on that, but can you just elaborate on what that means.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, some of the mass graves primary mass graves, or those first created were subsequently opened and some of the bodies moved. That happened in the case of Petkovci Dam, Kozluk, Glogova, Orahovac, 1 and 2, and they are indicated by the italics and also Branjevo Military Farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I notice that some of the graves have different names. For example, Orahovac is also called Lazete 1 or Lazete 2. Can you explain why?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's just effectively a process of the time that these graves have been exhumed. Initially we believed the area of Lazete, for instance, was referred to by local people as Lazete. We then learnt that it was the area of Orahovac. And it seemed appropriate to change the name to what was appropriate, given the local knowledge and also indicated on maps. The dam was referred to colloquially as the red dam and later on we identified the area as Petkovci. So we called it the dam at Petkovci or near Petkovci. So it was simply a process of correctly identifying the area where the graves were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, turning then to the map which is mounted. It's Exhibit 55 for the record. Can you using the pointer identify for us -- I'm assuming that's going to come up on everybody's screen, the primary disturbed mass graves.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: At the top of the map Branjevo Military Farm, this primary grave has been disturbed; the grave at Kozluk has been disturbed; the primary grave at the dam near Petkovci has been heavily disturbed; the graves at Orahovac, which is known as Lazete, have been disturbed; to the south of the map, the grave at Konjevic Polje 1 and Konjevic -- sorry, Glogova 2 and Glogova 2 have been disturbed. The remaining primary graves indicated in red had not been disturbed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't believe we were able to see the south of the map on the screen, but hopefully the Chamber is able to see it from the map itself that is mounted. Now, you also have on the legend of the map, which is at the very bottom, the notation of the execution points, which are indicated with black circles, such as, for example, Kravica warehouse to the south of the map and to the very north, Pilica Dom. Can you -- starting with these execution points, can you indicate where they were in relation to the primary mass graves.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Pilica Dom is at the very top of the map. It's a short distance away from the Branjevo Military Farm. The Kravica warehouse is to the south and it's on the road between Konjevic Polje and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you now indicate the undisturbed sites, the undisturbed primary mass graves.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Those sites are in the south. They include Cerska, what's known as Nova Kasaba 1996, Nova Kasaba 1999, Konjevic Polje 1, Konjevic Polje 2, and what's known as Ravnice 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the legend of the map also indicates that these secondary mass graves are marked with green circles. Can you just go through all the secondary mass graves and what their connection is to the primary mass graves for us.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, the group of graves along Hodzici road - the seven graves - I indicate that grave 1 was not used. There's strong indications that those -- three of those graves were connected to Orahovac or Lazete. Moving down to Cancari road --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I stop you there for a moment. You said there were strong indications, there were arrows connecting Orahovac to these three graves. Just very briefly - we're going to get to this in more detail - can you indicate how those graves were connected.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had experts examine in this particular case the soil pollen samples within the primary grave and that found within some of the secondary graves. A match was found to that indicating that the soil in the secondary graves had come from the primary graves. Also we found cloth blindfolds and ligatures which were examined by experts and shown to match from the primary grave to the secondary grave. We also found shell cases within both types of graves, the primary and secondary. Those shell cases were examined by experts and shown to match. And those indications show us that the grave, the mass grave at Orahovac was linked to the three secondary graves in Hodzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on then to the next primary grave, the dam near Petkovci, can you show us how it's connected to which secondary grave and how.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The dam at Petkovci, which was a large primary grave on the embankment of a dam, again analysis of soil samples in relation to the primary grave matched those at one of the secondary graves at Liplje road. There are four graves along that road and it was found to match the exhumed secondary grave of Liplje 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Kozluk, the primary grave of Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The Kozluk grave which is on the banks of the Drina river was shown to be disturbed and it was connected to the primary grave that was exhumed at Cancari road 3. If you see, it's again the soil and pollen samples as I described, blindfolds and ligatures, again the same; shell cases the same. But also we found broken -- large amounts of broken green glass and bottle labels at Kozluk which were also located at Cancari road 3 which was completely exhumed. The other secondary graves on Cancari road were probed and we located green glass in one of those graves. But it was not fully exhumed so we don't know if there were bottle labels there. But those bottle labels match a bottling factory near the Kozluk mass grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And moving on to the primary grave at Branjevo Military Farm, it appears to be connected to Cancari 12. Can you elaborate on that.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's the mass grave at the top of the Branjevo Military Farm was found to be disturbed and on examination of Cancari road 12, soil and pollen samples as described samples match the primary grave and also blindfolds and ligatures which were examined matched the primary grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then moving on to the southern part of the map looking at Glogova, the primary grave of Glogova, how is that connected to the secondary grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's two mass graves at Glogova which are separated by a small roadway. Examination of those graves indicated to the majority had been disturbed. We were able to connect that -- those two graves to the secondary graves at Zeleni Jadar road which were Zeleni Jadar 6 and Zeleni Jadar 5. Again, through soil and pollen samples and shell cases. We were also able to link that -- those two primary graves to the execution point at Kravica warehouse, and this was done through artifacts from the warehouse which matched the artifacts found in the primary mass grave and also the secondary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get into that a little more detail later on, but can you give us an example of the nature of the artifacts that matched?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: There were a number of pieces of masonry and brick, steel, part of the supporting beam for the front door, effectively the front door of the warehouse was found in the Glogova graves, along with painted pieces of masonry and supporting material from the building which matched the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Before leaving the map I notice on the map there are a number of secondary subgraves. For example, if you look at the southern-most point of the map of -- looking at Zeleni Jadar, there appear to be seven subgraves associated with Zeleni Jadar. Now, can you explain -- can you explain that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Along that stretch of roadway there were located seven secondary mass graves, which had been created roughly at the same time. They were dug on sides of the road or in some cases away from the road. Two of those graves have been exhumed, a third has been tested and found to have been emptied, and the other three graves have not been exhumed by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what significance was it that two of them had been tested and had found to have been emptied?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: One of the graves, Zeleni Jadar 2, was examined by the chief archaeologist was found to contain evidence of being used as a mass grave such as minor body parts and other evidence which indicated it had been used. But there were no bodies in the grave, which suggested to the expert that there had been a tertiary grave created. In effect, the bodies from that grave had been removed and placed somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before leaving the map, Mr. Manning, can you indicate what is the approximate distance between Srebrenica, which is to the south, and Branjevo Military Farm, which is the northerly-most primary grave site.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I think directly it would be about 80 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've been to this area before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. I've been to each of the mass grave sites indicated on the map and also the execution points indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far would it take to drive from Srebrenica to Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's a difficult estimate, but an hour and a half, probably more earlier on. But it depends on conditions. It's quite a -- it's quite hilly around Srebrenica, but maybe an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are the factors that indicate that a grave site is a secondary grave site as opposed to a primary grave site? How is it determined which graves were created first?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, specifically we had survivor testimony which indicated when some of the primary graves had been created. We also had aerial imagery provided by the U.S. government, which indicated approximate dates as to when the graves were created. They showed before and after shots, if you will, of the area before the grave was created and then after the grave was created, which indicated that they had been created at or after the time of the Srebrenica massacres. Subsequently those graves were -- seemed to be disturbed, again by aerial imagery. They were shown to have been opened, dug up. At the same time, areas removed from the primary graves were disturbed. Again, aerial imagery showed those areas that had been disturbed. They coincided with the time that the primary graves had been disturbed. But effectively they were secondary because they weren't created at the time the primaries were created. And following investigation, we found them to be linked. Therefore we described them as secondary to the primaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps we can go through some of the aerials to demonstrate what you've just indicated. Turning to Exhibit 566. Can you identify what we're looking at there.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is a map produced to aid the Chamber. It shows the area of Bratunac and the Konjevic Polje road leading from Bratunac to the left of the screen. The two red circles indicate the primary graves of Glogova 1 and Glogova 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to the next exhibit, 567.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is an aerial image. Again, these were provided by the U.S. government. It shows an area just off the Konjevic Polje road, which would be to the top of this photograph. On the right-hand side of this photograph marked as GL-1 is the primary grave of Glogova 1. And on the left-hand side, the bottom side of the road, is the other grave of GL-2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 568. Can you tell us what that depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is a photograph looking from the roadway which separates the two graves, and it's looking towards the primary mass grave of Glogova 2. It's the disturbed area of soil next to the man that can be seen in the left of the photograph. In the foreground is a grave marker, which was as I understand it associated with some of the houses that were there. It was a historic grave marker. But that shows the area of the primary grave prior to exhumation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is Exhibit 569. Can you indicate what that depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Again, this is an aerial image of the Glogova 1 grave, the one on the right-hand side of the road. It indicates the date of the 27th of July, 1995, on the left. And then on the right in October of 1995, it shows the disturbance of that site. It shows what's indicated as trenches. It also shows an excavator working, apparently working at that site. I indicate that myself and the archaeologists, the chief archaeologist, used these photos to identify and commence the exhumation of both the Glogova 1 and Glogova 2 graves. Effectively we used such photos to identify the outline of the grave and where we should commence digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 570. Can you indicate what that image depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is another image from the 30th of October, 1995. It's a much clearer image. It clearly shows the disturbance of the two sites. You can see what appear to be track marks. You can see what appears to be a hole and a spoiled heap of soil and, as indicated, a machine at the site. Again, these images were used by the archaeologists on the site to assist them in determining where the graves were and the history, if you like, of the disturbance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 571. In the series of exhibits, it's the last one. What does that depict, Mr. Manning?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is an image from November of 1995. Again, it's the same series of images provided by the U.S. government. It indicates the two graves in winter, effectively. You can see the outline barely where the depression caused by the graves marks the snow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then moving on to another primary grave by way of example, the Orahovac grave. The next exhibit is 572.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Again, this map is to assist the Chamber in placing the Orahovac, Lazete, grave. To the right of the circle is Zvornik. In the top is the dam near Petkovci. The red circle is Orahovac. And if you follow the road below it to the left, it would travel back towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 573 is the next one. What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Again, a U.S. aerial image. It shows the before and after shots of the Orahovac 1 and 2 mass graves. If you see on the left-hand pane in the 5th of July, 1995, there's no disturbance available. On the right-hand side pane on the 27th of July, at the top centre of the picture is a disturbance with vehicle tracks, or it looks like vehicle tracks. Moving down the photo to the bottom and below the railway line is a large disturbance heading into the woods. They -- this photograph depicts the creation of the primary grave at Orahovac 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning then to Exhibit 574. What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is a close-up of the Orahovac 1 grave which was the one at the top of the photograph. In the left you can see the area in September of 1995. And whilst the area is disturbed, you can see that it's perhaps starting to grow back. On the right-hand side on the 27th of September, you can see that there has been a disturbance of that site. The site has been enlarged and there are what look to be vehicle tracks throughout that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the significance of that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Effectively this shows the grave on the left after it had been created and prior to a disturbance, prior to being dug up. And on the right-hand side it shows the grave after it's been dug up and it looks as if it's been closed again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to the exhibit 575. Can you tell us what that depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is the second grave, Orahovac 2, which is behind the railway line. You can see in the top of the photograph a railway line. Again, 7th of September, it shows the site as it stood then. And the 27th it shows an area which has been disturbed again and what look like vehicle tracks throughout that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving then on to the next primary grave, which is Branjevo Farm, exhibit 583.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is another aerial image provided by the U.S. government. It's marked as Branjevo state farm, which we know is Branjevo Military Farm. It's dated the 17th of July. It has a number of markings on it which indicate various structures and things on the ground. Of particular interest is an area in the centre left of the photograph, which shows a number of bodies on the ground, a large number of bodies. To the bottom left of that photograph is an excavation, a mound of soil, and clear vehicle tracks from the bodies to the area of the mass grave. It also shows an excavator or a machine parked at the site and the various buildings which make up that site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, that was actually Exhibit 584. Exhibit 583 was the map. We don't need to go through that. The next exhibit that we will look at in the series is 585.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is another photograph of the Branjevo Military Farm, and it shows effectively the same area. However, it shows the burial area of the grave to the bottom left of the photograph. It indicates a disturbance of that grave and the associated vehicle tracks with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving then on to Exhibit 586. What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Again, it's the same area of the military farm. And highlighted in an expanded square is the words "backhoe" and "frontloader," which indicates a machine at the site. And the mass grave to the bottom left of the photograph is described as a newly excavated trench. And again, you can clearly see vehicle tracks surrounding the grave and leading from and to the grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And by way of example, we're now going to look at one of the secondary graves. Exhibit 587. Can you just indicate, Mr. Manning, what that depicts, briefly please.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This shows the area of the Zeleni Jadar mass graves. It shows the graves 1 to 6, which is situated south, directly south of Srebrenica. I would indicate that the point which is marked I, Zeleni Jadar 1 actually, consists of two graves. The grave wasn't probed at this stage. But effectively it is a probed unexhumed grave, so it would be 1A, 1B, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So seven graves along that stretch

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just by reminder, that grave, Zeleni Jadar, was connected to which primary mass grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The exhumed graves at Zeleni Jadar 5 and 6 have been connected to the Glogova 1 and 2 mass graves and hence to the execution point at Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving then on to Exhibit 588. Can you indicate what that aerial imagery depicts?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is a collage of two images from the U.S. government, and it shows the area along the Zeleni Jadar road which has been used for the secondary graves. As indicated, Zeleni Jadar 1 is two graves and you can see two disturbances there. And as you follow the road along you can see disturbances on the side of the road which represent the secondary graves. Zeleni Jadar 2 is the empty grave. Zeleni Jadar 3 and 4 have not have exhumed. 5 and 6 have been exhumed by ICTY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to Exhibit 589, what does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is again a before and after aerial image. It's dated the 7th of September, 1995, and the 2nd of October, 1995. And if you see the exact same image left and right, there's no disturbance in September the 7th. However, on the 2nd of October, it's clearly visible that there are two disturbances, what look like open pits. The Zeleni Jadar 1 grave is, if you'd like, what we would call 1A. The -- if you go to the bottom centre of that right-hand pane, you see another disturbed area. In 2001 I was present while that grave was probed, and we located multiple human remains in that grave and designated that as Zeleni Jadar 1B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning then to Exhibit 590. Can you indicate what that depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This shows that same area. And on the left-hand pane, on the 18th of October, you can still see that it appears to be an open pit. On the 20th of October, it appears that those two pits, 1A and 1B have been covered up or closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just briefly, Mr. Manning, what is the significance of that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Well, given the fact that both those graves were examined and found to contain multiple human remains, this indicates that sometime on the 18th of October to the 20th of October, the bodies were placed in those graves and those graves were then sealed until we came and probed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on then to Exhibit 591. Can you indicate what that depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Again, this is a split image of the roadway adjacent to Zeleni Jadar 2 mass grave. On the left-hand pane of August 24th, 1995, there's no disturbance. On the 2nd of October, 1995, you can see clearly a pit. I would indicate that that grave, as I said, was the one that had been robbed or disturbed. And very adjacent -- very close to that grave is the river. I think you can see it in this image. It runs right alongside the grave. And in fact, when I visited that grave, it was being flooded by the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said that grave was the one that was robbed or disturbed. Can you just clarify specifically what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: "Robbed" is a term used by the archaeologists. But it indicates -- as the primary graves have been robbed or disturbed or opened or removed or the contents removed, in a similar way, Professor Richard Wright indicated that Zeleni Jadar 2 had been robbed, that is the contents had been taken somewhere else and the grave had been filled back in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving then to Exhibit 592, can you indicate what that exhibit depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: It's another in the series, if you like. The previous one had shown before the grave was created and after it was created. This shot shows the grave when it was open. And on the 23rd of October or thereabouts when it had been sealed again. So we assume that between the 20th and the 23th, bodies had been placed in the grave and the grave sealed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This again is the Zeleni Jadar 2, which you indicated earlier was emptied?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to Exhibit 593, can you indicate what that exhibit depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: It's the same stretch of road. It's not far from Zeleni Jadar 2. On the left-hand pane, the 7th of September, 1995, no disturbance. And on the right-hand pane on the 2nd of October, 1995, the grave of Zeleni Jadar 3 had been created.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And has that grave since been exhumed yet?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: No, that grave was not exhumed by ICTY. It was handed over to the Bosnia Commission for Missing Persons. And I don't know if they have yet exhumed that grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then to Exhibit 594. Can you indicate what that depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is the same area and it shows the Zeleni Jadar 3 grave as it has been covered up and closed, assuming that the bodies had been placed inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then to Exhibit 595. That depicts what?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Exactly the same process. In this, the panes are split top to bottom. In the top pane you can see that there is no disturbance. On the bottom, you can see that Zeleni Jadar 4 to the top of the road has been created. And Zeleni Jadar 5 on the curve of the road has been created. I was present at the commencement of the exhumation of Zeleni Jadar 5. Zeleni Jadar 4 has not been exhumed by ICTY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to Exhibit 596. That exhibit depicts what?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Again, this image is showing the secondary graves after they had been filled in. The date is the 18th of October, 1995, Zeleni Jadar 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then to 597.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is the final grave along the Zeleni Jadar roadway or area. On the 7th of September, 1995, there is no disturbance. On the 27th of September, 1995, there is a -- an elongated open pit which has been excavated and it's designated Zeleni Jadar 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then to Exhibit 598, the last in the series.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This shows the 12th of October, 1995, on the left-hand pane. Clearly the grave is open. And on the right-hand pane on the 18th of October, the grave has been closed after being filled with bodies. There is vehicle tracks along and around that grave. I used that image and similar images when I was present at the opening of that grave, Zeleni Jadar 6. We used those images to find a grave, locate the edges of the grave, and exhume that grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Manning, just to save time. We're not going to go through the remainder of the aerials. But during the course of your involvement in this matter you've actually had a chance to review all these -- all the aerials on the exhibit list. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. I've reviewed all the aerial images available to us. I've also used them, as I indicated, in the field to identify mass grave sites and assist in their exhumation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your review of the remainder of the aerials, were you and the investigation team able to determine the creation dates of the graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, within the ranges indicated on the photographs. I can't comment on the days that these were taken, but clearly between the 12th of October and the 18th of October, this grave was filled in. We also were able to match the disturbance of the primary graves, the opening of the primary graves, and the opening and closing of the secondary graves. But those two things occurred at the same time. The primaries were opened and disturbed. The secondaries were created and then filled up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honours, Exhibits 576 through 582 relate to the primary graves, the dam and Kozluk. And exhibits 599 through 645 relate to the secondary graves of Hodzici, Liplje, and Cancari. So in the interest of saving time, I do not propose to refer to these at this point, but I will be seeking to tender them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then to another area, Mr. Manning. You indicate, Mr. Manning, when a grave is initially identified, what are some of the factors that indicate whether a grave has actually been disturbed or tampered with?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: In most instances we were assisted significantly by the aerial images which had indicated that disturbance. And using those images we were able to see a disturbance on the ground. I've indicated vehicle tracks which were present. You could see those vehicle tracks. You could see where a fence line perhaps was knocked down to allow entrance for a vehicle. So they were very useful. But specifically the evidence of disturbance of the graves was indicated by the archaeological examination of the site. The archaeologists were able to examine the soil composition, the structure, the layering, et cetera, and determine that the grave had been determined, the original features and formations of that grave had been broken into or dug through. And in some instances it was very clear to a layman, such as myself, including areas where bodies had clearly been removed, sections of bodies had been cut through, and that mass of bodies were missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to some of the exhibits, Exhibit 549/107. Can you indicate, Mr. Manning, what this photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken during the exhumation process at Kozluk mass grave. What it shows is the top of the photo a group of bodies. They're laying on the original surface of the ground. And that surface would have continued down through the bottom of the photograph. But you can see what -- this section of the soil which has been removed. You can see the wheel ruts from a machine. You can clearly see the teeth marks from an earth-moving machine to the right of the photograph and in the base of the photograph. And if you look where the bodies meet the area of disturbance, you can see that those bodies have been bisected, they've been cut through, and that mass of bodies which would have continued down the photograph have been taken from that mass grave and removed. You can see quite significant disturbance to the base of the soil, as I say from the wheel ruts. And it's clear that that happened after the bodies had been placed on the soil, thus showing that the disturbance happened after the people had been placed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning then to Exhibit 653. Can you indicate what that photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is part of an expert report prepared by Professor Richard Wright. And it details exhumation of the Glogova 1 mass grave. I was present for a significant part of this exhumation and I saw these features in the grave. The left-hand photograph indicates tooth marks from a machine which had dug through the soil, leaving the imprint of the teeth and the blades from the machine. It also is shown in photograph in the middle which you can see to the centre, slightly left, marks through the soil where the machine has cut through the soil. When soil is put on top of that, it preserves those marks. And the archaeologists have been able to remove the soil and show the marks. On the right-hand side of that image is clear vehicle tracks in the base of the grave. You can see the fact that a wheel or wheels moved across the surface of the soil. And again, I was present and saw these marks in the base of the graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning then to Exhibit 652. Can you describe what this photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This is one of the graves, subgraves if you like, of GLO1. It's the bottom of a deep pit in which a number of bodies have been placed. The bodies were removed in this image. And this body remained at the base of the grave. And the body is resting on top of the marks or the teeth marks made when that grave was initially created. If you like, they dug the hole, leaving the teeth marks in the soil. They dumped this body on top of that, so obviously it post-dated the creation of the hole. And then further bodies were deposited on top. This grave was robbed and there were indications further up the hole of disturbance of the wall of the grave, showing that it had been robbed. And this young individual was left in the bottom of the grave to show that effect, that the grave had been created and that he had been placed on top of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. According to the information that you received, Mr. Manning, excuse me, does this -- is there any indication what kind of device had been used on the bodies in the various photographs that we've just seen?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: If you mean what device was used to dig the graves or to rob the graves, in this instance, because it was a deep pit, it was indicated to me and demonstrated to me that it was probably a machine such as a -- called a 360 digger, a machine with an arm that can reach into the soil and pull soil up. The other disturbance on the previous exhibit was caused by, in part, by a similar machine but a machine with a blade or a bucket which would reach into the soil and lift the soil up and take large parts of the soil out. This indicates two different machines. And each of the graves that were exhumed, we were able to identify such features and in many instances indicate what type of machine was used, general type of machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the effect of the removal process on the bodies in the primary grave and the evidence that is associated with those bodies?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The effect of opening up the primary graves and disturbing those bodies, transporting them and placing them in secondary graves, is that it severely hampered our efforts to even count the bodies let alone identify the bodies or provide a cause of death. If you have an undisturbed grave such as Cerska, there were 150 male individuals killed in that grave. It was easy to identify the sex. It was easy to identify the cause of death. It was easy to identify the number. When you go to the Kozluk grave or the Glogova grave or any other primary disturbed graves, bodies are broken up, bodies are separated, bones are smashed. And the bones, identification material, artifacts are distributed across the primary grave, spread by the machine. They are also distributed across the secondary sites, spread across the sites by the machines, broken up, and the loss of the evidence is significant and the damage to the bodies was very significant in hampering our investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Manning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we are now going to show a nine-minute video depicting part of an exhumation which is by way of example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Manning, the scenes we are about to watch, can you indicate who videotaped them?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I videotaped them, and I apologise for the quality. I recorded them at the exhumation of the Orahovac 1 mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I'm asking the assistance of the AV booth to play the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do we have to watch it from the very beginning to the end?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's only nine minutes, Your Honour. So we've shortened it actually; we're not going to play the entire tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If there's some explanations by this witness, I think it's okay. But I have received that videotape already and watched it already in my office. So you may try it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honour's hands. If you prefer I don't play it, that's fine. I do believe Mr. Manning was going to provide some further explanation in addition to what is already on the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that will be okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this section of the video indicates a bullet which has been located and the process of handling the exhibits, marking them with a number issued by the scene of crime officer and then photographing that item in situ before it is bagged and placed into evidence. This shows the mechanical digger working at the site, which scrapes the top layer of soil off. Two men watching are archaeologists and they are attempting to see artifacts or body parts which may be disturbed. This is a body which has been located and is being exhumed. You can see a cloth blindfold on the skull of that body. You can see the bags which have been labelled to accept artifacts located from that body. Measuring and photographing survey points taken from that body, which is number 290. This shows the process of removing the body and body parts. The person conducting the work is an anthropologist, as are all the people handling the remains. This shows the removal of the body parts piece by piece. It indicates the slow and meticulous nature of the work which has to be conducted in relation to each of these bodies. This shows the continuing process of metal detecting over and under the body to identify metal artifacts any danger to the people, but also bullets embedded below the body or on the body. Once the body is removed or parts of the body are removed the archaeologist continued to find the bottom of the soil, to make sure there were no other remains or artifacts below the body. That body bag is then transported to the mortuary. This is another body within that same grave. They've located the cloth blindfold on the head of that body. This is another area of the grave which is being exhumed. It shows again the time-consuming effort involved in exhuming each of these bodies. It also shows the different states of preservation from the previous body. This is the same grave, and it was being exhumed five years almost to the day since the bodies had been placed in the grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I thank the AV booth for assisting us with that in the videotape. If I didn't indicate earlier, Your Honour, that was Exhibit 654. It is 10.15 as I see on the clock, and I believe it may be time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for the break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Manning, turning then to the general findings of the experts and firstly dealing with statistics, I believe that you prepared a chart in relation to that, a table of results, which is at Exhibit 649. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. I produced a table of results from the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many individuals were found in total in relation to all the graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: This figure represents a minimum calculation of that number. I don't believe it represents how many we found but it represents a minimum calculation of the number of bodies accounted for in the graves. That has been assessed by an expert at 2.541 individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say a "minimum calculation," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: As I said before, with the disruption of the bodies, with the breaking up of the bodies, and the spreading across sites, it makes it very difficult to count the number of individuals. Because of that, anthropologists have to assess the number of individuals represented in the bodies or body parts or bones that we find. They do that by counting a specific type of bone until they come up with a figure that they say would represent the smallest number of individuals in that mass of bones and bodies. That was calculated by Mr. Jose Baraybar and recalculated over the years. And as the primary graves were exhumed and matched together. He then combined all the figures for the primary and secondary graves and produced a figure which he says is the -- represents all the bodies from all the sites combined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that figure was the 2.541 that we see in the second column marked MMNI at the very bottom. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is MMNI? What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Normally the figure -- the acronym is "minimal number of individuals," but because Mr. Baraybar was asked to join all the primaries and all the secondaries, whether they were connected or not, he used the term "minimal minimal number of individuals."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your report, which is the latest report of 2003, which was Exhibit 554, I believe you indicated that the total number of bodies was 2.571. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain the discrepancy between what you have in your report and the 2.541 minimal minimum of individuals?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: There's two main reasons for that difference, one being in my report I based the figures that I had on the work of Mr. Baraybar before he amalgamated all the sites. But also some of the sites hadn't been examined by Mr. Baraybar by him. He hadn't produced an MNI for those graves. So I had to rely on the next best figure, if you like, which was an assessment of the number of complete or almost complete bodies by the chief pathologist, Professor Clark or Dr. Clark. Therefore I was adding two different sets of figures because one definitive figure was not available. The second reason for the difference of approximately 30 individuals was in comparing the different sites which were exhumed over different years by different people using methods which have progressed or changed, Mr. Baraybar sought to identify bones or specific types of bones which were represented right across the sites. The process of doing that meant that he had to eliminate some individuals who were represented in the graves but didn't have the correct or right bone for him to assess. In effect, he sought the lowest common denominator, and when that denominator wasn't present he effectively was forced to ignore some of the bodies. It wasn't a significant number. As I said, about 30. But that's why his figure is 2.541. The previous figure that I produced based on his report -- sorry, his work and the work of the pathologist was 2.570.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this figure of 2.541, is that considered to be a conservative figure or a liberal one?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: It's a very conservative figure for the reasons I've outlined, particularly with Mr. Baraybar's assessment. But also had we not used the amalgamation of all the graves, the MNI by its very nature is conservative. It seeks to represent the minimal number of individuals in the grave. If the bodies are broken up, if the bodies -- certain bones are missing, if the bones that you want to count aren't represented or you can't distinguish the bones from each other in that you don't want to double count, you use an MNI and it is a very conservative figure. And from my experience with the autopsy process, I believe it significantly undercounts the number of bodies that are represented in the graves that were exhumed. The ultimate number of bodies will hopefully be determined through the DNA analysis being conducted by the Bosnian Commission, in which almost every bone will be examined and identified. And that will provide the definitive number of bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us a -- perhaps a practical or concrete example of how the MNI is calculated in the sense of -- you're saying, for instance, there is a bone -- specific bones are counted. Can you give us an example of that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm conscious that I'm giving this as a layman's point of view, but I have discussed it at length with the experts and I believe I came to an understanding of it. If you have ten complete bodies in a grave, then it's ten bodies. If you have ten bodies complete and one skull, then clearly it's 11 individuals. You can continue on like that, but if you, say, found that you were counting the left thigh bone because it's a large bone and we all have one -- normally have one left thigh bone, you could count all the left thigh bones in that group of bodies if you didn't have complete bodies. If you counted ten left thigh bones, it would indicate ten individuals. However, if you found a right thigh bone you wouldn't normally count it, unless that right thigh bone was perhaps from a female and all the other ten were males or was from a child. If that bone, that different bone was significantly top the ten that you already counted, you could then count that bone. So you would have ten left thigh bones, you'd have one right thigh bone, then you might have a skull that wasn't represented by those thigh bones, different sex or different age. Therefore, that process continues by the anthropologist until they come up with a figure that they can represent as the minimal number of individuals. But again, if the bones are broken up, if the bones aren't complete, you have to be very careful that you double -- you don't double count. Therefore, you tend to exclude a large number of body parts and bones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, the figure you're referring to 2.541 is found in Mr. Baraybar's latest report, Incident 660, which was produced in January this year. Now, this figure, 2.541, does that take into account the unexhumed graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: No that simply represents the number of graves that we've exhumed, the 23 mass graves. It doesn't take into account the secondary graves that we handed over to the Bosnian commission and did not exhume. It doesn't take into account the logical tertiary grave from Zeleni Jadar 2. It doesn't take into account other primary graves that we believe exist from witness testimony but we have not located. And it does not take into account other secondary graves we are aware have been created but not yet probed or examined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have there been archaeological estimates made of the unexhumed graves that obviously have been located?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Professor Richard Wright who examined seven secondary graves in 1998 made a calculation in his report of that year's work in which he made an estimate of the number of bodies which were likely or possibly to be found in the secondary graves as yet unexhumed. He based that on the -- a simple average of the graves that have been exhumed, the lowest and the highest. He took the average. And he produced an estimate of, I believe, 122 point something bodies per unexhumed secondary grave. On that basis, he came up with a figure of I believe 2.571 bodies which would be represented mathematically by the unexhumed graves. That didn't take into account Zeleni Jadar 1B which hadn't been -- been located. So he produced that figure based on the known secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was in the exhumations that occurred as of 1996 -- or 1998, rather?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That was based on his work in which he not only exhumed the seven secondary graves in 1998, but he probed all of the secondary graves which -- the 20 other secondary graves. So based on his examination of the ones he had exhumed and the examination of the ones he had probed and examined the aerial imagery and the dimensions of the graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Manning, if we were to take a concrete example of the Zeleni Jadar graves which we saw earlier on the map, I believe there are approximately seven of the subgraves -- seven subgraves, are you able to give us an estimate of the number of individuals in the secondary graves that have been unexhumed?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, simply applying Dr. Wright's estimate, there are two graves along that road which have been exhumed. There is one grave which is empty, which leaves four secondary graves unexhumed. Using that rough estimate of 120 individuals, we would expect there to be in the region of 480 to 500, I suppose, bodies in those unexhumed graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And looking at the table of results that is on our screen, if you added the -- that estimate of unexhumed graves to the exhumed graves of Glogova, which was approximately 613, according to the MMNI, what are the estimated number of bodies that are located at that site?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Simply adding that number 613 plus 480, say, you are over 1.000 individuals, which would likely be represented in the exhumed graves, primary and secondary, and the unexhumed graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a connection made between the Glogova and a particular execution point?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. As I said before, the Glogova 1 and 2 primary graves were clearly connected to the nearby massacre at the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And going back to Richard Wright's total estimates of the secondary unexhumed graves, which I think you indicated was 2.571. If you add that to the number of exhumed individuals, what is the estimated total number of bodies for all the graves?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object here for one second. I understand that there were some qualifications by the gentleman. He's indicated that they are estimates made by someone else, not by himself. So I just want to make sure that we understand that these are just guesstimates based on some probability that was calculated by some other individual who, as I understand it, will not be testifying here. So I don't object to them guessing as to what the final number would be. But I want to make sure that not a whole lot of weight be placed on this number unless they can produce the gentleman here to be cross-examined who made these guesstimates or some other ways that we can sort of rely on this figure. So as far as it being just a guesstimate, I don't have a problem. But I want to make sure that my objection is registered as far as the weight that should be given to these figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think your objection is registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond to that by way of reminder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Richard Wright's report and his testimony from the Krstic trial has been admitted pursuant to 92 bis and 94 bis. Pursuant to this Chamber's ruling as of 7 November 2003. So that evidence is before the Court. So I would submit that the weight should be placed accordingly as you would place any weight on any other witness's testimony, given that it is before the Court and it has been admitted by this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think both parties have put their hands into our domain. And at this stage I'm only going to say that I hope the witness could bear in mind the objections from the Defence counsel and answer the question put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, bearing in mind those comments, if you add Mr. -- Professor Wright's estimate of 2.571 to Mr. Baraybar's calculation of 2.541, obviously it's in excess of [Realtime transcript read in error "2.500"] 5.100 individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure that was registered in the transcript, the last number that -- the figure you gave, Mr. Manning. Could you just please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The number presented by Mr. Baraybar in his calculation was 2.541. Mr. -- Professor Wright's calculation was 2.571. An addition of those two is roughly 5.100 plus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in addition to the unexhumed graves, Mr. Manning, how many unknown graves are there believed to exist?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's a difficult question because we don't know what we don't know. But one witness and it may be before --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's being asked to speculate and his answer is quite clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, believe to exist, which means that this witness may have some information to believe there exists some graves. Let's hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Just as long as we understand that he is now going to be speculating to some degree based on witness testimony as opposed to some other concrete evidence such as satellite imagery, as they have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may answer this question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There may be testimony before this Chamber by a survivor of the execution at the dam who indicated a trailer full of bodies was conveyed away from the site, indicating the existence of a grave. We have attempted to locate that grave; we have been unable to. As I said the Zeleni Jadar 2 grave had been emptied, indicating a tertiary grave. We have been unable to locate that grave. And I am aware of testimony before this Chamber or investigative material deriving from testimony, which indicated another three graves. One of those graves, to my knowledge, has been probed by the Bosnian Commission and multiple human remains located. So in specific answer to that question, I would say there are five other graves that we don't know about or don't know the location of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And have there been any more recent findings of graves to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, as I indicated, I think only recently one of three suspected sites was probed or tested by the Bosnian Commission and multiple human remains were located in that one grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to the Ravnice grave, Mr. Manning, do you have the estimates as to the number of bodies located in the Ravnice grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I would -- to be completely accurate with the Chamber, I would prefer to refer to the table. There are a lot of figures and I don't want to mislead you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was Exhibit 649 that's currently on our screen.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, the two graves at Ravnice are described as Ravnice 1 and 2. Effectively they are one grave, but because we, ICTY, exhumed partly Ravnice, we called it Ravnice 1. The next year the Bosnian Commission for Missing Persons continued that exhumation, monitored by the ICTY; therefore, we called it Ravnice 2. In the ICTY preliminary exhumations, 34 individuals were located following 198 individuals were located. Using Mr. Baraybar's formula of calculating and merging those two sites, because they are the same site, he calculated that number to be 219.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything else you can tell us about those graves, the Ravnice graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: The Ravnice graves were unusual in the fact that they were closely located near the Glogova 1 and 2 graves, but they were up a roadway. And the bodies had been dumped down a cliff. It had appeared that the bodies had been pushed off the cliff and had scattered down the cliff face. Some of them had been stopped by trees, some had wrapped around fence posts and wire. And there -- I was present at the exhumation by ICTY and part of the exhumation by the Bosnian Commission. And there were distinct groups of bodies and they were angled away from the road. The experts at the exhumation accounted for that by trucks being -- dumping bodies down the cliffside and the angle being caused by a narrow road. Some attempt had been made to cover some of the bodies. Some soil had been taken from the other side of the road and dumped over those bodies. Not all the bodies had been covered. And because of the slope and because the bodies had been skeletonised, a large proportion of the body parts had rolled down the cliff into the valley, making it very difficult to collect all the remains. Also on the examination we -- sorry, the autopsy of the bodies collected by the ICTY and by the Bosnian Commission was conducted at the ICTY morgue. On examination, the majority of those bodies were found to have been -- the cause of death of multiple gun shot wounds. There weren't, if I recall correctly, a significant number of blast injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any evidence connecting the Ravnice mass grave to a particular execution site?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, there was. During the exhumation by the Bosnian Commission and whilst I was present, artifacts which were identical to those at the Kravica warehouse were located. A startling piece was one of the -- part of the foam lettering from the doorway of the warehouse was located in amongst the bodies at Ravnice. And on examination the foam lettering above the doorway at the warehouse was -- seemed to be missing that part. It was clearly to the experts that there was some connection between the Ravnice grave and Kravica. Large artifacts were not located, however.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just briefly going back to one point, if the Zeleni Jadar graves were covered by October 20th, which is what we saw in the aerial imagery earlier, and the Glogova grave was still open or being dug up by October 30th, according to the aerial imagery, do you know where bodies were taken from Glogova on the 30th of October?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then to the issue of gender. What gender were the majority of the victims found in the various graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Gender was assigned as either male, which the majority of the victims were identified as male, or undetermined was a significant number of individuals. There was one positive identification of a female which was in the Konjevic Polje 1 mass grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. With respect to age, was it possible to determine the age of the victims in the graves?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. That was part of the aim of the autopsy examinations. The age ranges are detailed in the various reports of the experts. And because of the different experts and the different systems applied, there are assigned age ranges. So rather than assigning a specific age to an individual, they were often assigned quite broad age ranges. The age ranges tended to be from the very young -- younger than 12, 12 to 19, right up until quite old individuals in their 90s.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By way of example, Mr. Manning, can you give us the age range of the victims in Glogova 1.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I can with reference to my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps with leave of the Court, the witness can refer to his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And while the gentleman is looking at the report, just again -- and I certainly don't mind taking two or three days with this material. However, if a lot of these reports have been brought in through 92 bis and as the Prosecutor -- all of them have argued continuously that the Defence is wasting time by asking questions, I don't see why we need a summary witness to summarise 92 bis material that has been entered by the Court. Again, I don't object I don't want to seem as if I'm trying to minimise the impact or -- of the gentleman's work. But again, if the essence is on the part of the Prosecution simply to sort of inflame the situation more than it is, then I would object to this. Because a lot of this material has come in through 92 bis, then it's there. And There's no need to be using this witness just to summarise 92 bis material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in principle, I agree with you, Mr. Karnavas. But on this particular question, I think to refresh the memory of this witness, the witness is allowed to make some reference to his report. Of course there is no need to re-introduce those reports again. And in this situation, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you have the full right to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. Of course we've always maintained that these incidents occurred. We haven't challenged the grave sites. But I do understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, since the Defence counsel, I believe two of them, have already indicated that they did not challenge those facts. So maybe you could further streamline your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will do my best, Your Honour. That was -- the last question was simply by way of example. I wasn't going to go through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Manning, have you found that reference?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and I can be brief. Of the bodies autopsied at Glogova 1, excluding those from grave L which we don't need to go into for the interests of time. One individual was determined to be between 13 to 17 years of age, four individuals between 15 and 24 years of age, and 19 were in the 25 plus category.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this information is contained in which report, just for our -- for ease of reference?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
