utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were there any aerial imageries that you are aware of or examined with respect to the Cerska grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, there were aerial images of the Cerska grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the dates of that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I would have to check the images, but the creation date was the 13th of July, 1995. Because the Cerska grave was -- they were pushed down a slope and soil was taken from the other side of the road, what you see on the image is that mass of soil taken from the side of the road and dumped on top of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we would be able to look at this aerial imagery and sort of get a ballpark figure as to -- at least some kind of indication when this incident might have occurred at the very latest, maybe not when it actually occurred, but we would have -- we would know that up until this time something occurred?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, again with the others, there's before and after photographs, and, yes, they would show when it wasn't disturbed, and the window, and when it was disturbed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you produce those for us at this point. Could you tell us whether they are accessible -- well, first let me ask you this: In preparation for today's testimony, did you -- because I noticed that you pointed to aerial photographs, there were other photographs of a variety of nature, including a warehouse that we have seen on a number of occasions, did you by any chance inspect the aerial photographs for the Cerska graves -- grave?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If it would be of assistance, we do have the aerials that were entered through Mr. Ruez's testimony and we could certainly provide those if it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, let the witness answer the question first. And then we'll see whether the Defence counsel needs that photo or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, I inspected that aerial image along with many of the other aerial images.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That was in preparation to come here today. I'm not talking about whether you did that when you first arrived, but I'm saying in preparation for today because I know Ms. Issa prepares exquisitively [sic] hard for her presentations so I'm sure she had you there proofing, going over all the documents, and as we saw it was almost a flawless presentation thanks to Ms. Stewart. So the question is: In your preparation to come here today, did you look at those?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes, or in recent preparation for the Milosevic appearance in relation to the same matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And as I understand it, you are no longer working on the Srebrenica case?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was -- when did you stop working on the Srebrenica case?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I took up my duties with team 4 on the 9th of September, 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have a couple of questions, Your Honour, and I think I will take about 30 to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have all of tomorrow. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, we can start tomorrow if that pleases the Court better. Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Manning.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted in the first segment of my questions to direct your attention to the primary grave Kozluk. Did you personally participate in the exhumation works at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not. I had visited Kozluk. I had seen some body parts sticking out of Kozluk, and I wasn't present at all for the rather lengthy exhumation of that grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to our information, that exhumation was done in two parts, the first one was in June 1996 and the second time was in August 1999 and they were performed by Professor Rickt [as interpreted]. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honour, Kozluk was exhumed in 1999 by Professor Richard Wright. It was not exhumed previously. It was apparent that there were body parts on the surface of the grave. One or two of those body parts were collected I think in 1998 and were examined at the mortuary and then were retained for inclusion with the rest of the exhumation. But it was only exhumed once in 1999 by Professor Richard Wright and his team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your report that was submitted here, I'm talking about Exhibit -- that is your statement for this trial. It was done in two parts, namely in June and August 1999. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I would like to check the specific section, but it was conducted over about a six-week period or a seven-week period, so it would have been June and August of 1999. But I would have to specifically check that, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means in para 13 of your report, Kozluk, the grave was exhumed in June and August 1999 by an ICTY team led by Professor Richard Wright?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. I perhaps see the confusion. It was over that period. They started in June and they finished in August. It was a continuing process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you said that from the findings you received you drew the conclusion that the executions were carried out on the site where the mass grave was detected. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, on what basis did you draw that conclusion and does it hold true of all bodies, of some of the bodies, in other words, on a part of the grave or the entire grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, it holds true for a large number of the bodies. I would have to specifically check the report of not only Dr. Wright but the chief pathologist, Dr. Clark. But it consisted of bodies which had bullets underneath them consistent with them being fired through the bodies. It was consistent with bodies who were in a posture which indicated they had been shot as in falling forward with their arms bound behind them. In one graphic example, an individual had been shot across the back and he had, whilst still living, grasped a bush, the root of a bush, in his hand. And when he was exhumed, when the soil was taken away, his hand was still seen to be around the bush as it was when he died. That sort of evidence was what Professor Wright was able to identify. And again, finding the bullet holes and the bullets underneath the body indicates that they were killed at that site and then covered with soil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In August 1999 when the exhumation was performed, was that grave already robbed, were the bodies already reburied?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. That occurred in 1995. And if you recall the photograph that I showed the Chamber of the teeth marks and the bodies that were bisected, that is the Kozluk grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how many bodies were found in the primary grave in Kozluk in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Without checking the table, I think it was 380 or a similar number. I've checked the table from Mr. Baraybar, and it was assessed at 340 individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have information as to how many bodies were in the primary grave in Kozluk, because -- before parts of the bodies were removed, in other words, or was the total number of bodies initially buried at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I believe that is addressed in Richard Wright's report, but over 150 were recovered in the associated secondary grave at Cancari road. And it is a very large area, a very large grave, but that is addressed, I believe, in Mr. Wright's report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're asking these questions for one simple reason: We would like to remove one dilemma. Namely, is it possible that bodies were brought to the primary grave in Kozluk? In other words, could there have been bodies of people who were not executed there, at least some of them, according to your analysis?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I don't believe that's the case, and it's not supported by the archaeological examination, in that they showed that there was a large number of bodies spread over the surface of the soil, a large number executed in situ, and then the soil had been dumped on top of them. If those bodies had come from different sources from outside the Kozluk execution point, you would expect to see that reflected in the archaeological condition of the bodies. There would be a difference in the bodies. There would be, you would expect, material, as you see in the secondary graves, collected from where the bodies died. That material wasn't visible. You could see that the bodies were laying on a surface and that they all appeared to be simply sitting on the surface, laying on the surface, and that there was a consistency to those bodies. If they had been brought in in a mechanical digger or a truck, you would expect to find evidence of that, a pile of bodies or other material; that wasn't found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware of testimony which says that those bodies were found in a pit that used to be there earlier and that had been dug to get gravel. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would agree with that. The whole area is a collection of pits and piles of gravel. And significantly, piles of broken green glass. And a number of the bodies in the photographs and the descriptions indicate that those bodies were on top of that green glass or on top of that surface where, as you say, the gravel would have been moved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that the grave was not actually dug in the place where those bodies were found; rather, an existing pit for the exploitation of gravel was used to bury the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: I've seen the topography maps and I've seen the photographs of the grave as it's been completely exhumed. I wouldn't agree that it was a pit, but yes, it took part, it used the existing landscape, which as you could see was a sloping face where material had been removed. I can't agree that it was a classic pit, but it was an area or three areas which had previously been dug for whatever. The bodies were laying on that surface and down the slopes. And then the bodies had been covered up by soil which had been taken from nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That's exactly what we wanted to get at. Mr. Manning, let us clarify one small for the record. Did I understand you correctly when you say that parts of the shards of glass which emanate from the factory nearby were under the bodies, not above the bodies exhumed in this location, in this primary grave?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were large fields of glass. And it was put to me that a lot of the bodies were on top of that glass and that they were killed whilst resting or kneeling or laying on that glass, on that field of broken glass. Yes, there was green glass below the bodies and also in the surrounding area. There were thousands and thousands of pieces of broken glass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that glass was in that location even before the bodies were brought. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And machinery was used to remove a layer of earth from the vicinity, a layer which covered the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING
utterances.text: Yes. There was evidence during the exhumation of what they would call the spoil pit or the place where the soil was taken and dumped on the bodies. And it was also reflected in the aerial image or images.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I should like to ask you some questions about a location called Rocevici, which was not covered either by your map or your analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, though, that this is a good moment to stop, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So tomorrow you could start with the new areas of cross-examination. And we'll resume tomorrow afternoon at 2.15 in Courtroom III. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
